- When sentiment is negative (avg < 0) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 73), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above peak or align with 30d moving avg.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3 consecutive negative sentiment values), model underreacts — add 2–3% upward bias to forecast.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — add 1–2% to forecast for first 5 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast with 3-day moving average before final output.
- If true outcome is consistently 1–2% below forecast, model is overconfident — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 30d horizon.
- If sentiment is positive but price declines, model fails to adjust — add 1–2% downward bias to forecast if sentiment > 0.3 and price drops > 1% from prior day.
